content.text: {"quote_faithful": "yes", "verdict": "confirmed", "evidence_kind": "missing_justification", "fatal": "yes", "explanation": "The quoted sentence appears verbatim in the \"Current best\" section and is indeed empirical (\"Empirically...\") and speaks of eventual periodicity, conditioned on an unproved finite-core claim. Scanning the whole text: the sections are \"Approaches tried\" (numerical data for a1=15, 35, prime powers), \"Key observation\", a \"Conjecture\", and \"Full proof: (Not yet complete.)\". Nowhere is L defined as a specific product of primes with a proof that membership in the admissible set is invariant under m -> m+L for all m >= a_1, nor is T defined as the count of terms in a window of length L, nor is a_{n+T}=a_n+L derived for every n >= 1 (the text even flags circularity concerns). So obligation (P) is entirely absent, and without it the required conclusion is not established."}
